standard_prerequisites.name: Integrality transported along a ring map
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used to divide an integrality relation by powers of f (lines 7823-7829)
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the localised integral closure is contained in the integral closure of the localisation.

standard_prerequisites.name: Clearing denominators in an integrality relation over a localisation
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces a single element of the multiplicative subset that makes the numerator integral over the source ring.

core_obligations: Show containment of the localised integral closure: divide an integrality relation for x in B' by powers of f to obtain one for x/f in the localisation (proof lines 7822-7829).

Conversely, start from an integrality relation for x/f over the localisation with coefficients a_i/f_i, and clear denominators with a suitable f' to exhibit f' f_1 ... f_d x as integral over A (proof lines 7830-7842).
Conclude that x/f lies in the localised integral closure (proof lines 7842-7843).
proof_roadmap: Divide an integrality relation to get one for a fraction (proof lines 7821-7829).
Clear denominators in an integrality relation over the localisation to come back (proof lines 7830-7844).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a ring map from A to B and a multiplicative subset S of A, the integral closure of S^{-1}A in S^{-1}B is the localisation of the integral closure of A in B (statement lines 7813-7819). The proof does not argue with the module of integral elements: one direction divides an integrality relation by powers of the inverted element, and the other clears denominators with a suitable factor from S to convert an integrality relation over the localisation into one over A for a multiple of the numerator (proof lines 7821-7844). The clearing of denominators is the substance, and the author displays both relations in full. H2.
